neighbours.label: ice skating / ice hockey context, on the token just before an ice word (rink, skater, hockey terms); the output promotes ' sk', ' ice', ' skating', ' hockey', ' puck'
fire: On Saturday mornings the children take skating lessons at the local rink.
The town council voted to build an indoor ice rink beside the school.
The winger scored on a slap shot from the top of the faceoff circle.
She has been a figure skater since she was six years old.
The Canadiens killed off the penalty and then scored on the power play.
The goalie made forty saves and the Oilers won in overtime.
He laced up his skates and stepped onto the frozen pond.
The puck slid along the boards and into the corner behind the net.
quiet: On Saturday mornings the children take swimming lessons at the local pool.
The town council voted to build an indoor tennis court beside the school.
The winger scored with a low drive from the edge of the penalty area.
She has been a competitive gymnast since she was six years old.
The Dodgers escaped the inning and then scored on a sacrifice fly.
The keeper made nine saves and United won in extra time.
He laced up his boots and stepped onto the muddy field.
They spent the week skiing down the long runs above the village.

notes: Card: ' the', ' r' (rink), ' sk', ' ice' in hockey and skating text. Probes: 'outdoor ⟦⟧rink' 0.86, slap shot 0.74, 'ice rink' 0.71, power play 0.44; soccer, swimming, baseball ~0.
